entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and plain: the thing has simply gone slack from repetition, a flatter judgement than the arch *bromidic*.

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hardest word in the family - it does not merely note the overuse, it writes the thing off as worthless for it.
examples: his remarks were trite and commonplace

entries.definition: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest of the group: the wear is admitted and half forgiven, where *threadbare* would call it ruin.

entries.definition: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps a straight face while it convicts - dull, wearying and puffed up with significance, all named at once, where *corny* simply laughs.

entries.definition: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and mocking: both the dullness and the airs come off as laughable, lighter on its feet than *platitudinous*.

entries.definition: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The drier of the pair - it names the tiresome self-importance almost clinically, without the heavy roll of *platitudinous*.

entries.definition: dull and tiresome but with pretensions of significance or originality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A weightier, more sonorous word than *platitudinal*, and its own bulk is part of the mockery: dullness dressed up and then shown up.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain term of the family - it reports that something hurts, in the body or in the mind, without saying how sharply or how much.

entries.definition: causing a dull and steady pain
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Low and unbroken - a pain with no edge on it, the opposite of the sting in *biting*.

entries.definition: causing a dull and steady pain
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal where *aching* is plain, and the shortened shape keeps the same dull, steady pain small.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Turned outward - it describes the look or the cry that shows pain, agony included, not the thing doing the hurting.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling of *agonized* and identical in force - distress made visible rather than inflicted.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Far past *aching* - the pain is extreme, and the word lends it agony's whole weight.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling of *agonizing*, with the same extremity and no softening.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The absolute of the set - it admits no degree above itself, so anything short of unbearable is overstated by it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Extremity felt as an ordeal - where *excruciating* measures the pain, this measures what it costs whoever goes through it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Extremity cast as an act - the pain is not merely present but done to someone, which *excruciating* never says.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The quality without the agent - pain of the order torture produces, said of the experience rather than of anyone inflicting it.
